stock.counterargument: Gross profit is only 0.127 of total assets, which a generic quality screen would mark down — often because an acquisition left goodwill on the balance sheet rather than because of how the business operates. debt is 4.10× trailing operating cash flow, which leaves less room if conditions turn.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +0.6%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $63.64 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 120 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-28.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-04) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use
stories.excerpt: Gemini 4 Carbon is essentially a slightly better version of Argon.
stories.lead:
It’s almost like Google’s got something to prove after taking a break from releasing new frontier AI models earlier this year. Just two weeks after rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon. This isn’t the Flash model equivalent we’ve been waiting for but, rather, is an improvement on Argon, and like that model, Google is working on a staged release that could take a while.

Stop me if you’ve heard this one before: Google says its latest AI model reaches a new threshold in coding, agentic tasks, and scientific analysis. It’s so capable, in fact, that Google can’t let you use it just yet.

stories.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.
stories.lead:
KYIV, Ukraine — Like many tech entrepreneurs in Ukraine, Yaroslav Azhnyuk turned to developing drone warfare after Russia's 2022 invasion.

Drones have transformed the way wars are fought. Azhnyuk says artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable.

"When the other side has orders of magnitudes higher capabilities, it gives you an asymmetric advantage," he says. "It can make you 10,000 times more effective."

stories.title: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
stories.excerpt: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the crash occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.
stories.lead:
Transport minister Óscar Puente said a computer failure at about 08:30 on Wednesday morning led to the initial halt of six moving trains, including the two trains that subsequently collided.

"In the event of a system failure, the control centre takes over," he said, adding it was the control centre that decided to allow the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions.

That decision, Puente said, was made "under inexplicable circumstances". It resulted in the Renfe train crashing into the Iryo train, which was stationary on the tracks some distance ahead.

stories.title: Carney to push for closer ties at Canada-EU summit in Montreal
stories.excerpt: The term "associate member" is reportedly off the table as officials discuss deeper economic and defence ties.
stories.lead:
For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this coming two-day meeting in Montreal.

Thursday and Friday's summit will be closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.

Last month, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed "opening the door" to Canada for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.

stories.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
stories.excerpt: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.
stories.lead:
Spain's network of high-speed rail has been considered one of the nation's crowning achievements. It ranks second to China in track mileage in the world. Until this year, it had not endured a deadly crash since coming into service over three decades ago.

The collision Wednesday that turned a sleepy stretch of rail lined by olive groves into a scene of carnage came just four weeks before the country votes in a national election.

stories.title: State ballots let voters decide on abortion, taxes, transgender restrictions
stories.excerpt: Missouri voters could ban abortion - after they just removed a ban two years ago. California voters could tax billionaires 5% of their wealth.
stories.lead:
Whether or not they live in a competitive congressional district, voters in many states will be deciding on statewide ballot measures with a chance to make law themselves.

There are 145 statewide ballot measures on the November ballot, according to Ballotpedia, which tracks elections.

In some cases the questions were put on the ballot with petition drives by citizens frustrated with the actions - or lack of action - by their state lawmakers. In many cases, legislatures go to the voters with amendments to their state constitution.

stories.title: These are the House races to watch in the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
stories.excerpt: An NPR analysis finds 70 House districts where Democrats and Republicans are each investing more than six figures in advertising during the final few days of the election, including in deep red areas.
stories.lead:
In the final week of the 2026 midterm election, ad spending data suggests the core battle is less about stopping a Democratic wave in the House, and more about figuring out how high it crests.

An NPR analysis finds the final competitive House landscape is expansive, including 70 districts where both parties are investing at least six figures per district into their final days of messaging.

That includes more than $10 million each in toss up districts in Michigan, North Carolina, New York and Florida; seven figure ad buys in deep-red communities across Tennessee, Oklahoma and Arkansas and last-minute resources to districts where gerrymandering by Republicans could backfire.

stories.title: Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers
stories.excerpt: American auto companies say they are paying more for key components like computer chips, steel and copper — plus the fuel needed to transport their products.
stories.lead:
American automakers are reporting their third quarter earnings, and they're saying revenues are up, but they're also facing some serious headwinds.

Or as Mike Wall, an analyst at the automotive data company Mobility Global, put it: If this year was a book about the auto industry, "It would be a mix of suspense and thrills and maybe a little bit of comedy and a little bit of horror."

For the thrills: Auto companies are doing well when it comes to selling big cars and light-duty trucks. General Motors reported its sales of light-duty trucks rose 9% in the past year. Ford's F-Series trucks continue to be a company bestseller. Stellantis' pickup sales in the U.S. rose 34%.
